title: Microsoft is openly competing with OpenAI, Anthropic more than ever
excerpt: Microsoft pitched its own homegrown AI models, harnesses, and even a Mythos competitor on Wednesday, telling Wall Street it plans for continued growth.
content_html:
Microsoft is in a unique position as AI overtakes the tech industry. It’s one of the world’s largest cloud providers and software-as-a-service companies, while also holding valuable stakes in the two biggest AI labs, OpenAI and Anthropic.

Those incentives are starting to clash as Microsoft posts blockbuster financial results. The company just reported an extremely profitable quarter, with $90 billion in revenue and net income of $35.8 billion. For the fiscal year, which ended June 30, Microsoft reported $331.8 billion in revenue with a net income of $133.7 billion for the year.

And CEO Satya Nadella is not about to let the trajectory of Anthropic and OpenAI — which are expanding into applications and agentic infrastructure that could ultimately let them own customer relationships — derail that kind of cash.

Nadella has been preaching to enterprises to use multiple models and to stop relying on the frontier AI labs for the agentic harness/app layer.

Doing so is dangerous, he’s been saying, because it requires companies to share too many of their internal secrets with model makers of dubious trustworthiness. He knows his customers. Enterprise IT fears both data leaks and being locked into a vendor.

Now he has openly told Wall Street analysts during the company’s quarterly conference call Wednesday that this is an opportunity for Microsoft to sell customers its own homegrown models, alongside agents, AI security and more, while promising lower costs.

In other words, he’s pitching Microsoft as an alternative to many of the upscale services that OpenAI and Anthropic are developing for their own growth.

When UBS analyst Karl Keirstead specifically asked Nadella to weigh in on the open versus closed-sourced debate roiling the AI industry, and how Microsoft will benefit from it, Nadella came out swinging.

“The goal is to have the firm be in control of their own destiny,” the CEO said of enterprises. “We are very, very clear about the architectural sort of design of the platform, which is you got to keep your harness separate from the model … that means any model at any given time is swappable.”

Microsoft, of course, sells a menu of harnesses (aka AI agents), too, under the Copilot name, including its coding agent GitHub Copilot. Coding agents are where much of the AI dollars are being spent today.

And he used the high-profile incident from last week as proof of his warnings.

“If you look even at the Hugging Face incident, the biggest thing that we should take away from that is you can’t sort of depend on any one model,” Nadella said. “You will maybe need multiple models to even remediate some challenges that get caused by one model. Like that’s the way to think about it, right? Which is you can’t be subject to a refusal of one model.”

The incident involved an unreleased model from OpenAI breaking out of its sandbox and successfully mounting a full-scale hack on Hugging Face, all in pursuit of besting a benchmark. Trying to understand what happened, Hugging Face at first tried to use a private frontier model (which it hasn’t named) that refused to help it. So it turned to the Chinese open source model Z.ai GLM 5.2 to analyze logs and defend its infrastructure. The incident has so shocked the industry that even Sam Altman is now saying that maybe AI development should slow down a bit.

Nadella also made clear that Microsoft is happily selling its own homegrown models, the MAI family, on its own homegrown AI chips, Maia, and pitching them as cheaper alternatives.

“Every customer wants the right model for each task based on quality, latency, cost, and compliance. We offer the broadest model catalog in the cloud with over 11,000 models, including the leads from OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, xAI, as well as our own MAI family,” he said.

He added: “We’re also accelerating our own model development. We announced more than a dozen new models across image, voice, transcription, coding, security, including our first reasoning model, MAI thinking one, all with cost-efficient inference at the core for the enterprise use cases. We are co-designing these models with our silicon, and we are seeing 40% better performance per watt when running MAI models on Maia 200.”

As for Mythos? Nadella pointed to Microsoft’s new Mythos competitor announced earlier this week, MAI-Cyber-1-Flash. It “achieves better performance than the much larger Mythos model, but at half the cost when combined with our multi-agent security harness,” he said.

Sure, the Microsoft CEO says that enterprises should use the frontier models that OpenAI and Anthropic offer in their mix. But his bigger message is: don’t trust them enough to rely on them.

content_html_zh:
随着人工智能超越科技行业，微软处于独特的地位。 它是全球最大的云提供商和软件即服务公司之一，同时还持有两个最大的人工智能实验室 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的宝贵股份。

随着微软公布惊人的财务业绩，这些激励措施开始发生冲突。 该公司刚刚公布了一个极其盈利的季度，收入为 900 亿美元，净利润为 358 亿美元。 在截至 6 月 30 日的财年中，微软公布的营收为 3,318 亿美元，全年净利润为 1,337 亿美元。

首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉 (Satya Nadella) 不会让 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的发展轨迹——它们正在扩展到应用程序和代理基础设施，最终让他们拥有客户关系——破坏这种现金。

纳德拉一直在向企业宣传使用多种模型，并停止依赖前沿人工智能实验室的代理工具/应用程序层。

他一直说，这样做是危险的，因为这要求公司与可信度可疑的模型制作者分享太多的内部秘密。 他了解他的客户。 企业 IT 既担心数据泄露，又担心被供应商锁定。

现在，他在周三的公司季度电话会议上公开告诉华尔街分析师，这是微软向客户销售自己的本土模型以及代理、人工智能安全等产品的机会，同时承诺降低成本。

换句话说，他将微软视为 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 为自身发展而开发的许多高端服务的替代品。

当瑞银分析师卡尔·凯尔斯特德 (Karl Keirstead) 特别要求纳德拉就人工智能行业中的开源与闭源争论以及微软将如何从中受益时，纳德拉的态度摇摆不定。

“我们的目标是让公司掌握自己的命运，”这位首席执行官谈到企业时说道。 “我们非常非常清楚该平台的架构设计，也就是说你必须将你的线束与模型分开...... 这意味着任何型号在任何给定时间都是可以更换的。”

当然，微软也以 Copilot 的名义销售一系列工具（又名 AI 代理），包括其编码代理 GitHub Copilot。 如今，大部分人工智能资金都花在了编码代理上。

他用上周备受瞩目的事件来证明他的警告。

纳德拉说：“如果你看看“抱脸”事件，我们应该从中吸取的最大教训是，你不能依赖任何一种模式。” “您可能需要多个模型来解决由一种模型引起的一些挑战。 这就是思考问题的方式，对吧？ 也就是说，你不能拒绝某一型号。”

该事件涉及 OpenAI 的一个未发布的模型突破沙箱，并成功对 Hugging Face 进行全面黑客攻击，所有这些都是为了超越基准。 为了了解发生了什么，Hugging Face 最初尝试使用私人前沿模型（尚未命名），但效果不佳。 因此，它转向中国开源模型 Z.ai GLM 5.2 来分析日志并保护其基础设施。 这一事件震惊了整个行业，甚至萨姆·奥尔特曼现在也表示，也许人工智能的发展应该放慢一点。

纳德拉还明确表示，微软很高兴在自己的本土人工智能芯片 Maia 上销售自己的本土模型 MAI 系列，并将其作为更便宜的替代品。

“每个客户都希望根据质量、延迟、成本和合规性为每项任务找到正确的模型。 我们在云端提供最广泛的模型目录，包含超过 11,000 个模型，包括来自 OpenAI、Anthropic、Mistral、xAI 以及我们自己的 MAI 系列的领先模型。”

他补充道：“我们也在加速我们自己的模型开发。 我们发布了十多个涵盖图像、语音、转录、编码、安全性的新模型，包括我们的第一个推理模型 MAI 思维模型，所有这些模型都以企业用例的成本效益推理为核心。 我们正在与我们的芯片共同设计这些模型，在 Maia 200 上运行 MAI 模型时，我们发现每瓦性能提高了 40%。”

至于神话？ 纳德拉指出了微软本周早些时候宣布的 Mythos 新竞争对手 MAI-Cyber​​-1-Flash。 他说，它“比更大的 Mythos 模型实现了更好的性能，但与我们的多代理安全工具结合使用时，成本仅为一半”。

当然，微软首席执行官表示，企业应该在其组合中使用 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 提供的前沿模型。 但他更重要的信息是：不要过于信任他们而依赖他们。
